## US Equities Fall for Third Consecutive Session as Treasury Yields and Oil Prices Rise

Three consecutive sessions of equity weakness driven by rates and oil is a macro regime signal that compresses multiples on long-duration tech names; if Treasury yields continue to climb, high-multiple AI infrastructure and semiconductor names face the sharpest valuation headwind in the portfolio.

- US stocks declined for a third straight session (per headline)
- Rising Treasury yields and oil prices are cited as the primary macro headwinds
- BABA, AAPL, CRWD, and others are named as 'in focus' — market-wrap context, not company-specific catalysts
- The cross-asset pressure pattern (rates plus commodities) suggests the headwind is broadening rather than isolated
